text: Cucaita is a municipality located in the Central Boyacá Province, within the Boyacá Department of Colombia. Its urban center lies on the Altiplano Cundiboyacense, approximately 20 kilometers (12 mi) from Tunja, the department's capital. It shares borders with Sora to the north, Tunja to the east and south, and Samacá to the south and west. The name Cucaita originates from the Chibcha language and can be interpreted as either "Seminary enclosure" or "Shade of the farming fields." Prior to the Spanish conquest, the region was inhabited by the Muisca people, who were part of the loose Muisca Confederation, and Cucaita was governed by the zaque of Hunza. Modern Cucaita was established on August 12, 1556, by friar Juan de Los Barrios. The primary economic activities in the area include agriculture, especially the cultivation of onions and peas, livestock farming, and minor carbon mining. The geographical coordinates are 5°32′N 73°27′W (5.533°N 73.450°W).
